tasks.short: Enter approved copy and format typography, columns and spacing for print.

steps.what: Retrieve approved copy, production plan and style guide from the {DOCS}.
Type or paste approved text into {OTHER} publishing software.
Set fonts, type sizes, column widths and spacing in {OTHER} publishing software.
Adjust line breaks, text fit and visual balance in {OTHER} publishing software.
Compare the text proof with approved copy and accept formatting corrections.

tasks.design: Bind approved copy in the {DOCS} to governed templates in {OTHER} publishing software, removing separate retyping. Configure paragraph styles, text fitting and proof checks; the desktop publisher handles visual exceptions and accepts the checked text layout.
tasks.previous_blocker: Copy arrived in inconsistent files, and local formatting overrides weakened reusable styles.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing import and style features handle repeat formats. AI coding reduces the effort of building source adapters and comparison scripts.
tasks.still_hard: Complex tables, multilingual typography and dense pages still need skilled composition.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when technically correct typography makes the message harder to read.

ambition.what: Large-print editions for readers with low vision

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from text entry to composition exceptions and reader testing. The publisher gains delegated authority to choose typography within approved accessibility and brand limits.

reach.task: Check whether layout changes alter meaning or reading order.
reach.learn: Proof marks, textual comparison and reading-order checks.

evidence.claim: Governed templates can generate layouts from supplied content.
Native imports, paragraph styles and preflight rules can remove repeated text entry and formatting.

assumptions: The initial scope covers one recurring publication family with approved styles.
Approved copy can be imported without changing its wording.
GDPR applies to personal data in source files; access and retention follow the publication purpose.
EU AI Act obligations depend on the deployed use. Consultation follows applicable national rules.
unknowns: Which import and proof-check features the existing {OTHER} publishing software supports.
How often copy changes after layout begins.
Whether employee consultation is required under applicable national rules.
research_questions: Which import formats preserve paragraph structure and language-specific typography most reliably?
new_work: Maintain style mappings and template versions.
Test font changes and accessibility variants.

tasks.short: Create sample layouts, refine the strongest options and obtain design approval.

steps.what: Gather the production plan, populated layout and style guide from the {DOCS}.
Build sample page arrangements in {OTHER} publishing software.
Select and refine sample layouts for hierarchy, balance and audience fit.
Send sample proofs and an approval request through the {EMAIL}.
Review sample proofs and approve a direction or request changes through the {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: A generator fills a small set of governed layouts in {OTHER} publishing software and checks fit against the production plan. The publisher refines the strongest samples, while the {WORKFLOW} routes versioned proofs from the {DOCS} to the marketing manager for design approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reusable layouts existed, but producing alternatives and tracking feedback still required manual file handling.
tasks.enabler_now: Template rendering and approval routing are established capabilities. AI coding makes it cheaper to connect them and add fit checks.
tasks.still_hard: Original art direction, conflicting stakeholder preferences and unusual formats resist fixed templates.
tasks.human_edge: Choose the visual argument that serves the audience and explain that choice to stakeholders.

ambition.what: Compare two audience-specific layout directions at each campaign kickoff

tasks.altitude: The publisher spends more time comparing visual directions and less time assembling samples. The publisher gains authority to shortlist options; the marketing manager retains design approval.

reach.task: Develop layout concepts around a campaign message.
reach.learn: Visual hierarchy, concept rationale and critique methods.

evidence.claim: CHILI GraFx supports governed layout templates populated with content.
Versioned proofs and configured approval routing can replace manual circulation.

assumptions: Recurring sample requests share enough structure to justify a small template library.
Time shares include the marketing manager's review effort, excluding waiting time.
Sample approval selects a design direction; publication release is a separate action.
GDPR governs personal data in proofs and feedback. EU AI Act duties and consultation under national rules depend on deployment.
unknowns: How much sample work requires original design rather than existing templates.
Who has authority to approve each publication type.
Which rendering interfaces and review permissions are available.
research_questions: Which deterministic layout constraints best detect unreadable but technically valid samples?
new_work: Maintain a deliberately small set of layout alternatives.
Check rendered samples after template changes.
Resolve contradictory feedback and preserve the approved version.

tasks.short: Import approved text and artwork, resolve file problems and check placement.

steps.what: Find approved text and artwork in the {DOCS} and download working files.
Inspect file compatibility, resolution, colour profiles and recorded usage rights.
Import text and place artwork into linked frames in {OTHER} publishing software.
Adjust crops, scale and positioning in {OTHER} publishing software.
Check missing links, substitutions and visible import errors in {OTHER} publishing software.

tasks.design: An integration reads approved asset versions from the {DOCS}, builds a manifest and checks technical metadata and recorded permissions. Deterministic placement fills frames in {OTHER} publishing software; missing permissions, unusual crops and failed imports go to the publisher before acceptance.
tasks.previous_blocker: File naming, approval records and layout links were inconsistent across folders and incoming files.
tasks.enabler_now: File metadata, checksums and publishing scripts already support reliable import pipelines. AI coding lowers the cost of adapting them to local conventions.
tasks.still_hard: Missing rights records, damaged files and misleading crops require human resolution. Technical metadata cannot establish permission by itself.
tasks.human_edge: Preserve the intended meaning of an image and recognise when a crop changes its context.

ambition.what: Publication asset readiness report before layout starts

tasks.altitude: The publisher handles exceptions and advises requesters before production starts. The publisher gains authority to return incomplete asset packages with specific correction requests.

reach.task: Prepare consistent artwork packages for publication.
reach.learn: Colour management, effective resolution and asset provenance.

evidence.claim: Governed layout templates can be populated with supplied assets.
Metadata checks, version manifests and scripted placement are deterministic engineering patterns.

assumptions: The initial scope covers common supported text and image formats.
Missing or ambiguous usage records block asset acceptance and trigger review.
GDPR applies to identifiable people in images and associated records.
EU AI Act duties depend on any model use; consultation and employee image rights follow applicable national rules.
unknowns: Where approved assets and usage records are stored.
Which file formats cause most import failures.
Whether asset identifiers and publishing scripting interfaces are available.
research_questions: Which conversions preserve colour profiles, transparency and linked-file behaviour across supported formats?
new_work: Maintain format adapters and technical thresholds.
Resolve missing permissions and mismatched versions.
Retest placement after publishing software upgrades.

tasks.short: Interpret design instructions, resolve gaps and plan the production sequence.

steps.what: Collect the brief, design instructions and print specifications from the {DOCS} and {EMAIL}.
Read instructions and note deliverables, constraints, dependencies and missing information.

loop.input: The instruction package and a fixed publication requirements schema.
loop.output: A requirements checklist with source references, conflicts and explicit missing fields.
loop.check: Validate field types and source references; the publisher checks constraints and unresolved conflicts.
loop.stop: One extraction and one validation repair per package; unresolved items return to the publisher.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text briefs express constraints inconsistently; fixed fields handle structured requests but miss prose requirements.

steps.what: Discuss conflicting instructions, missing assets and deadline trade-offs with the marketing manager.
Choose the production sequence and checkpoints against clarified requirements.
Record the production plan and assign preparation tasks in the {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: A structured intake in the {WORKFLOW} captures standard requirements and gathers source documents from the {DOCS}. A bounded extraction loop prepares a referenced checklist for free-text instructions; the publisher resolves ambiguity and chooses the sequence, then configured automation creates the work queue in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Briefs mixed prose, attachments and late messages, while production dependencies stayed in the publisher's memory.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured intake and dependency templates cover routine requests. Bounded extraction can turn remaining prose into a reviewable checklist without deciding production trade-offs.
tasks.still_hard: Implicit expectations, conflicting deadlines and technically unrealistic requests need discussion and experience.
tasks.human_edge: Ask the question that exposes the real priority and negotiate a workable production commitment.

ambition.what: Assess production feasibility before each campaign brief is finalised

tasks.altitude: The publisher spends less time reconstructing instructions and more time advising at brief stage. The publisher gains authority to propose production options; deadline and scope changes remain with the marketing manager.

reach.task: Shape campaign briefs around feasible publication formats and deadlines.
reach.learn: Campaign objectives, scope negotiation and production capacity planning.

evidence.claim: Structured intake, dependency templates and configured routing can automate production paperwork.
Bounded extraction can draft a requirements checklist, subject to source validation and human review.

assumptions: Structured intake is preferred; only residual free text uses a model.
Conflicting instructions remain unresolved until a person clarifies them.
GDPR requires suitable access, retention and processing arrangements for personal data sent to a model.
EU AI Act obligations depend on deployment. National rules determine employee consultation requirements.
Build ranges cover a scoped pilot; consultation or access negotiations may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Whether requesters can adopt a shared intake form.
Which requirements are mandatory for each publication type.
Who may change scope, deadlines and resource commitments.
Which model-processing arrangements and employee consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: How reliably can referenced extraction identify contradictory instructions across documents and messages?
new_work: Review extracted requirements and missing-field alerts.
Maintain intake fields and dependency templates.
Evaluate extraction failures after brief formats change.
Maintain access controls and processing arrangements.

role.altitude: The role moves from repeated file assembly toward publication quality, accessibility and production advice. The publisher gains bounded decisions over typography, sample shortlists and asset readiness; marketing approval remains with the marketing manager.
reach: Graphic designer: develop and explain visual directions.
Proofreader: verify meaning and reading order after layout changes.
Marketing manager: assess publication feasibility while briefs are being shaped.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a publication readiness service that checks briefs and assets early, offers audience-specific layout directions and supports large-print editions.
